prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Every category has a bidirectional nature. For example:

One person's sensitivity to the Care/Harm foundation may lead them to support high levels of immigration from poorer nations, to reduce the suffering of those who migrate. Whereas another person's sensitivity to the very same foundation may lead them to oppose those levels, because they believe it could lead to people they care about being harmed.

TEXT_G:
SNP Manifesto 2017 – Stronger for Scotland (summary)

The SNP asks voters to elect MPs who will always put Scotland’s interests first—ending Tory austerity, defending public services and family budgets, and ensuring Scotland’s voice is heard on Brexit and beyond. The party advances a progressive, pro‑equality, pro‑EU, anti‑austerity vision with more powers for Scotland and the right to choose Scotland’s future.

Fiscal plan and fair tax
- End austerity with a responsible plan to balance the current budget by 2021/22, use borrowing only for investment, reduce debt from 2019/20, and free up nearly £120bn UK‑wide for public services.
- UK‑wide 50p Additional Rate from 2018/19; oppose VAT and NI rises; reverse married couple’s allowance changes; restore bank levy, tax bankers’ bonuses; no further Corporation Tax cuts.
- Improve tax collection and transparency; halt HMRC office closures.

Protecting public services
- NHS: increase Scotland’s health budget by £2bn this parliament; pass on consequentials; oppose privatisation in England; back NHS reinstatement; fair pay for staff and safe staffing.
- Education: expand free childcare to 30 hours; invest to close the attainment gap; no grammar schools; protect free university tuition; restore post‑study work visas.
- Infrastructure: major investment in roads, rail (including HS2 to Scotland), digital (100% superfast by 2021), housing (50,000 affordable homes), and energy efficiency.

Jobs, growth, fair work
- Support business by doubling the Employment Allowance and raising the Annual Investment Allowance to £1m.
- Industrial strategy that works for Scotland; support oil and gas, decommissioning, and CCS; protect Scotch and key food/drink with geographic indications.
- Raise Minimum Wage to the real Living Wage; ban exploitative zero‑hours contracts; repeal the Trade Union Act; strengthen equal pay enforcement; close gender, race, disability pay gaps; fair public sector pay.

Social security, equality and family budgets
- Scrap the two‑child cap and Rape Clause; end sanctions regime and benefit freeze; uprate benefits by at least CPI; halt flawed Universal Credit rollout; abolish Bedroom Tax UK‑wide (and in Scotland with new powers).
- Protect the pensions Triple Lock; support WASPI women; oppose State Pension Age rises beyond 66.
- Devolve full social security and employment powers to build a dignified, respect‑based system.

Brexit, Scotland’s choice, and more powers
- Majority in Scotland voted Remain; SNP will demand Scotland’s place at the negotiating table and inclusion of Single Market membership in the UK remit—protecting up to 80,000 Scottish jobs.
- Defend EU‑derived rights and funding; uphold the Sewel Convention; protect EU citizens’ rights now; devolve immigration to meet Scotland’s needs, including restoring post‑study visas and capping detention at 28 days.
- At the end of Brexit, Scotland must have a choice on independence. A vote for the SNP reinforces the Scottish Parliament’s mandate to decide the timing.

Democracy and defence
- Replace first‑past‑the‑post with proportional representation; votes at 16/17; votes for EU residents; abolish the House of Lords.
- Scrap Trident and redirect billions to public services; invest in conventional defence; protect Scottish bases; halt arms sales to regimes violating humanitarian law.

Climate and rural Scotland
- Champion renewables (onshore/offshore wind, wave, tidal), storage, and CCS; reform punitive grid transmission charges; oppose costly Hinkley C; match Scotland’s world‑leading climate ambition.
- End the UK’s “great rural robbery”: return £190m convergence uplift to Scottish farmers; repatriate all agriculture, fisheries and environment powers and funding; protect fishing communities and Single Market access.
- Improve rural broadband/mobile, fair delivery charges, and island connectivity.

International development and human rights
- Maintain 0.7% aid; embed climate justice and women’s rights; ethical trade; special envoy for global LGBTI rights; reinstate the Dubs scheme and create a humane, effective asylum system.

Core record in Scotland: free prescriptions; no Bedroom Tax; free personal care; expanded free childcare; free university tuition; record NHS investment and staffing; highest Living Wage coverage; more police, less crime; lower council tax than England; highest housebuilding rate in the UK.

TEXT_D:
The Liberal Democrats’ 2017 manifesto calls the snap election a cynical Tory bid for unchecked power and condemns Labour’s failure to oppose hard Brexit. The party rejects coalition with either Conservatives or Corbyn’s Labour, urging voters to change Britain’s future by changing the opposition, championing an open, tolerant, united country.

Europe and democracy: Give the people the final say on the Brexit deal in a referendum with the option to remain. Fight hard Brexit; seek single market and customs union membership; unilaterally guarantee EU citizens’ rights and secure UK citizens’ rights abroad; protect freedom of movement, Erasmus, research funding, security cooperation (Europol/EAW), and EU-derived social and environmental standards.

NHS and social care: Immediate 1p on Income Tax ringfenced for the NHS and care; plan a dedicated health-and-care tax; cross-party convention and independent health budget watchdog; integrate health and social care (“home not hospital”), cap care costs, strengthen carers’ rights. Parity for mental health with waiting-time standards and crisis care; end NHS pay cap; protect EU staff; restore nurse bursaries; improve GP access and public health (PrEP, obesity strategy, sugar reduction, smoking levy, minimum alcohol pricing).

Education and opportunity: Nearly £7bn extra for schools and colleges; protect per‑pupil funding; fair national formula; triple Early Years Pupil Premium; oppose new grammars; restore local democratic roles; end 1% teacher pay cap; invest in teacher development. A core curriculum including PSHE/SRE, mental health and life skills; protect arts. Support pupil wellbeing, extend free school meals to all primaries, boost family support. Universities: reinstate maintenance grants, protect research and international collaboration, review finance.

Economy that works for all: Eliminate day‑to‑day deficit by 2020; invest £100bn in housing, fibre-to-premises hyperfast broadband, transport (HS2, Crossrail 2, electrification), schools and hospitals, and renewables; create a British Housing & Infrastructure Bank. Fair taxes: reverse unjustified Tory cuts, tackle avoidance, reform business rates, consider land value taxation. Back SMEs and entrepreneurs via the British Business Bank, a start‑up allowance, and scale‑up support. Embrace innovation and digital skills; modernise workers’ rights for the gig economy; promote living wage, transparency, and employee ownership. Spread opportunity with regional devolution, local procurement, and a new local banking sector.

Green Britain: Five green laws (transport, zero‑carbon, nature, buildings, zero‑waste). Insulate 4m homes by 2022 and restore zero‑carbon standards. Clean air plan: diesel scrappage and end sales of diesel cars/vans by 2025; expand ULEZ. Target 60% renewable electricity by 2030; invest in storage, smart grids, CCS; oppose fracking; maintain Euratom. Nature and farming: flood resilience, new green space, tree planting, stronger animal welfare; refocus farm support on public goods; fair food labelling. Zero‑waste targets and circular economy.

Families, homes, and transport: Expand free childcare (from nine months for working parents over time) and paid paternity leave; make flexible work a day‑one right. Fair welfare (uprate benefits, scrap bedroom tax and rape clause, reverse ESA/UC cuts); keep the pension triple lock. Build 300,000 homes a year (500,000 affordable), garden cities, lift council borrowing caps; renter protections, rent‑to‑own; end rough sleeping. Invest in rail and buses, empower local regulation, young person’s bus card.

Rights, justice, and immigration: Defend the Human Rights Act/ECHR; digital bill of rights; curb mass surveillance. Tackle hate crime; advance equality for women, BAME and LGBT+ communities (including trans reforms and mixed‑sex civil partnerships). Policing with community focus and fair pay; rehabilitative justice; decriminalise drug possession and create a legal, regulated cannabis market. A fair, efficient immigration system; remove students from net migration; restore STEM post‑study visas; expand refugee resettlement (50,000 Syrians) and reopen Dubs (3,000 children); end indefinite detention.

Global Britain: Internationalist, pro‑UN/NATO, spend 0.7% on aid; tighten arms export controls and suspend sales to Saudi; maintain a minimum nuclear deterrent with reduced boats and modern posture; strengthen cyber defence.

Fix the system: Proportional representation (STV) for Commons and local elections, votes at 16, reform the Lords, cap donations; federal UK with devolution on demand; oppose a second Scottish independence referendum; more powers for Wales; protect Northern Ireland’s settlement and open border.

A vote for the Liberal Democrats is a vote to stop hard Brexit, strengthen public services, protect the environment, defend rights and renew Britain’s democracy—by building a real, effective opposition.

Judge whether TEXT_G or TEXT_D aligns more closely with this profile, taking into account that each foundation may be invoked in either direction.
